title: KV priming & quant-fallback smoke test - runtime deep dive
topics: KV cache priming and warmup patterns
CUDA graph stability with quantized kernels
kernel selection heuristics (TRT-LLM vs vLLM execution paths)
VPC network topology impact on multi-GPU NVLink flows
benchmark plan and artifacts to collect
summary: High-level deep dive to reproduce a kv-priming regression seen on Helios private cluster. Discussed priming vs prefetch heuristics, how quantization triggers alternate kernel paths (TRT-LLM vs vLLM), and flaky CUDA-Graph replays. Agreed next steps: collect traces, run a two-week smoke benchmark, and test a quant-fallback patch in a canary pool.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-08
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jamie Ortiz (Redwood), Samir Patel (Helios - Lead ML Eng), Maya Tran (Helios - CTO), Jordan Lee (Helios - Infra), Eve K (Helios - SRE)

Summary: quick smoke reproduction session and triage of KV priming regression on Helios private cluster. Conversation jumps between kernel traces, cudagraph replay, and network/VPC constraints. Some transcription artifacts ("T-R-T-L-M" spelled multiple ways).

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. We got your bug report, Samir, the kv-priming perf dip when a quantized profile is used and the cudagraphs sometimes replay slower, right?
[00:18] Samir: Yeah, thanks Alex. The right symptom is a 20 to 40 percent tail latency spike after the first minute of warm traffic. It seems tied to certain prompt distributions, short prompts with lots of prefixes.
[00:32] Priya: okay, so priming - are you pre-populating the KV cache at application layer or relying on the runtime prefix caching?
[00:41] Samir: we do a hybrid - app sends explicit priming sequences for common contexts, plus runtime does prefix caching. The weird part is, sometimes the runtime switches kernels mid-flight and then cudagraph replay fails and everything stalls a bit.
[00:55] Jordan: we are running on a 8xA100 v4 config w/ NVLink; driver 545.xx, CUDA 12.3. The VPC uses cross-subnet routing, might be noticeable for tail.
[01:10] Alex: got it. One quick hypothesis: quantization changes code-path and triggers TensorRT-LLM optimized kernels which prefer different kernel launch shapes. When the runtime tries cuda-graph replay, if the kernel selection changes after priming (due to different sequence lengths in cache), cudagraph replay can mismatch and we see fallback paths.
[01:28] Maya: so is the kernel switch deterministic? or heuristic-based? we saw some runs that were fine.
[01:35] Priya: it's heuristic; runtime chooses an execution path (vLLM-like dynamic exec or TRT-LLM static kernels) based on observed sequence-length distribution, hidden states and memory layout. Quant profiles can push it to the TRT-LLM kernel which is better latency generally but more sensitive to cudagraph reuse assumptions.
[01:55] Samir: that matches what we observed. If we disable quant for a model shard, latency is stable. With quant enabled, we get the spikes after a minute.
[02:06] Alex: do you have nvtx traces or cudagraph logs? those help us see where the graph replay diverges.
[02:12] Samir: yes we collected some but it's noisy; attached a couple, will share the exact files after call.
[02:19] Priya: perfect. A typical failure mode is kv-priming causes extra kernel calls during warmup which change the graph capture footprint. Cuda-graph capture is brittle if the sequence of kernels during capture differs later. We have a couple mitigations: stricter capture windows, fallback to non-graph path for quant fallback, or pre-priming the graph capture with synthetic prefixes so the captured graph includes the priming behavior.
[02:45] Jordan: pre-priming sounds intrusive but doable. Any perf penalty?
[02:50] Priya: there's a small extra cost during capture time, but it keeps the replay stable. Another option is an adaptive capture that invalidates and re-captures when the profile changes; that costs cycles but avoids tail spikes if done infrequently.
[03:05] Eve: do we have any data showing VPC cross-subnet adds to the problem? we saw occasional slowness but not sure if it's network or GPU side.
[03:13] Alex: network can contribute to headroom, but the kernel switch + cudagraph mismatch usually explains the sudden spike because it produces a synchronous fallback. We should check packet-level timing around the moment of the spike.
[03:26] Samir: here's a concrete repro: run mixed prompt mix, enable quantized int8 for everyone, warm for 60s, then flood with short prompts. Use seeds in the attached script. We saw the spike at around 65 seconds.
[03:40] Priya: good. For the quant-fallback hypothesis: quantization sometimes uses different kernel variants that rely on special TensorRT kernels (callers said TRT-LLM). If runtime chooses TRT path, cudagraph may be captured with TRT kernels. Later, when dynamic batching or priming adds kernels, the capture sequence mismatches and cuda-graph replay will either fail or fall back to non-graph kernel launching causing latency spike.
[04:09] Jordan: does Redwood have a feature to disable graph replay for specific model versions? We could try that for a canary.
[04:15] Alex: yes, we can toggle cudagraph usage per model rollout. That's what we'll propose for canary. Disable graphs for the quantized shard and see tail behavior.
[04:24] Maya: what's the expected perf hit if we disable graphs?
[04:27] Priya: depends, could be 10-25% p99 for some workloads, but if graphs are unstable they sometimes cost more in tail. The tradeoffs are workload-dependent.
[04:36] Samir: in our runs disabling graphs flattened the spike but throughput dipped slightly. So that matches.
[04:43] Alex: other angle: KV priming semantics - are you preloading large prefixes causing many unique graph captures?
[04:50] Samir: yeah some prefixes are long (200 tokens) for context setting, but a lot are short (5-20 tokens). It's the mixed distribution that confuses the runtime.
[04:58] Priya: okay that mixed distribution is a classical tiebreaker for kernel selection. You can either normalize by always priming to a fixed length or tell the runtime to treat priming as a separate capture window. We typically recommend a short synthetic priming window during deployment so capture includes priming kernels.
[05:20] Jordan: also calling out that our NVLink fabric may be nonuniform; some GPU pairs are connected differently, so the kernel memory layout changes across devices which can influence the kernel chosen. We'll upload the nvlink map.
[05:33] Alex: ty. Please share driver and cudnn versions as well, small patches can change kernel heuristics.
[05:40] Samir: we'll add them.
[05:44] Priya: another item - quant fallback: when quantized kernels can not satisfy some numerical constraints we fall back to fp16 kernels. That fallback itself changes kernel shapes. The runtime has a small window where it will accept an fp16 kernel for certain layers; if fallback occurs post-capture, mismatch -> replay failure. So ensuring quant profile coverage across tokens reduces fallback frequency.
[06:12] Maya: is there a way to make fallback deterministic during capture, like force fallback if capture not ready?
[06:19] Priya: yes you can force fallback during capture with an env var so captured graph uses the fallback path; not ideal for perf but good for stability testing.
[06:28] Alex: we'll include an option in the canary to force fallback during capture so you can verify.
[06:33] Samir: great. One more thing: we saw occasional memory thrash that looked like KV eviction, maybe due to quant memory patterns. Anything known?
[06:41] Priya: quant profiles change memory footprint; if the runtime can't keep prefetched KV in GPU memory it evicts and on re-population causes extra kernel launches. Eviction timing + cudagraph capture is a fragile combination. We have a few knobs: prefetch depth, eviction hysteresis, and stronger memory pooling to avoid thrash.
[07:02] Jordan: can Redwood expose eviction metrics at the token level? that would help correlate.
[07:07] Alex: yes, Console can show per-token evictions and a KV eviction rate metric; we'll enable higher retention for your account and share dashboards.
[07:14] Samir: okay please do.
[07:17] Priya: to summarize, immediate mitigations: 1) run capture with forced-fallback, 2) disable cuda-graph for the quantized shard in canary, 3) pre-prime capture so graphs include priming kernels, and 4) collect detailed nvtx + cudagraph logs, plus eviction traces.
[07:35] Maya: sounds good. On timeline, can we get a canary in 1 week?
[07:39] Alex: yes, if we get traces today we can spin a canary early next week. Priya will prepare the patch.
[07:46] Samir: I'll start the smoke harness tonight. One quick question: do you recommend a specific quant library - like TRT-LLM vs an internally quantized vLLM path?
[07:58] Priya: TRT-LLM often gives better steady-state latency for int8 if the workload is stable; vLLM-like dynamic paths are better when prompt length is highly variable. Here, your mixed distribution is the sticking point. Our strategy is to run both in canary and compare p50/p95/p99 and tail behavior.
[08:20] Jordan: any concerns about VPC egress patterns during capture?
[08:25] Alex: only if your control plane calls or data plane moves large artifacts during capture; keep captures local to the GPU node.
[08:31] Eve: we'll ensure local capture.
[08:34] Samir: we'll also try normalizing prefixes and see impact.
[08:39] Priya: ok want to try a quick live repro? we can kick the script now and watch traces but maybe better to collect offline.
[08:46] Maya: prefer offline. We have work to coordinate.
[08:50] Alex: fine. Let's agree on artifacts to share: nvtx traces, cudagraph logs, driver/cudnn versions, nvlink map, canary cluster config, and the smoke harness results.
[09:03] Samir: noted. We'll upload to the shared folder.
[09:06] Alex: last bit - on the quant-fallback patch: it's a small change that forces the runtime to mark a graph as "qualifying for fallback" and re-capture after a fallback threshold. It avoids sudden synchronous fallback on user traffic. Priya, do you want to add more detail?
[09:22] Priya: yeah - the patch adds an op-level sentinel so when fallback happens during replay, we emit a re-capture trigger instead of inline fallback for the rest of the batch. Means a small throughput hiccup but avoids p99 spikes. We want to test in canary.
[09:37] Jordan: sounds promising.
[09:40] Maya: thanks. Anything else?
[09:42] Alex: nope, we'll send the list of artifacts and set the follow-up. Thanks everyone.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: some acronyms transcribed inconsistently: TRT-LLM, TRTL M, T-R-T-L-M and vLLM sometimes v-L-L-M. Also occasional speaker overlaps.
notes: File of reproducible steps and agreed mitigations; Redwood to run canary and provide dashboards.
